reason: The text explicitly depicts the Hebrew people complaining about their leaders. Korah and his followers (250 men) assemble against Moses and Aaron, challenging their leadership authority. Dathan and Abiram specifically voice grievances, complaining that Moses has brought them from Egypt to kill them in the wilderness and is lording authority over them. They also complain that Moses has failed to bring them into a land of milk and honey or give them fields and vineyards. Furthermore, after the divine judgment, the broader congregation of Israel complains to Moses and Aaron, accusing them of killing the people of the LORD. This passage is fundamentally about dissent and complaint directed at the established leadership.
